title: The Struggle for Meaning Why the Fight Over AI Is Really About Who Gets to Speak
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
A public-facing political and labor essay by Lee Sharks presenting AI-mediated communication as a struggle over whose meaning is preserved, attributed, and heard.

The essay defines semantic extraction and liquidation in accessible terms, identifies content moderators, cultural producers, teachers, translators, care workers, oral-tradition communities, and misrepresented individuals as exposed groups, and connects semantic infrastructure to organizing capacity. It recommends clear attribution, consistent terminology, redundant publication, community archives, and shared movement vocabulary. Its claims that every online contribution enters training data, that contemporary systems privilege safety over attribution by design, and that specific retrieval interventions were already succeeding are broad or source-reported claims that should not be presented as universal verified findings.
